prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in League City, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1247; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my name on a recording, but you can use the claim reference.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the accident happened?
A: I was stopped at a red light on the main road in League City, near the shopping center.
Q: What was the first thing you noticed?
A: A loud bang, then my head snapped forward and back. The car behind me had hit me from the rear.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle coming before impact?
A: No. I was looking at the light. I felt the jolt and that was it.
Q: Were you able to get out of your vehicle?
A: Yes, but my neck was stiff right away. I sat in the car for a few minutes before I got out.
Q: Did you go to a doctor or an emergency room?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic the same afternoon. They said it looked like whiplash and gave me a neck brace.
Q: Are you still having symptoms?
A: Yes. My neck hurts when I turn my head, and I get headaches in the back of my head most days.
Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?
A: I missed two days and I've been working shorter shifts since then because I can't sit at the desk for long.
Q: Did you have any neck or back problems before this accident?
A: I had some stiffness from sleeping wrong now and then, but nothing that stopped me from working or driving.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I've been following my doctor's instructions and I'm going to physical therapy twice a week.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
A: Okay, thank you.
